business_scope.primary_industry_name: Visual Web Template and Low-Code Web Application Builder

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-France Double Taxation and Investment Protocol
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union bilateral investment treaty network
European Union investment protection framework applicable to Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended by the laws of 14 November 2004, 10 August 2018 and 25 January 2020); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the filing, access and control of UBO data.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing of foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or commercial court of the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police, passport authority or licensed notary of the jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or bilateral consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg notary and corporate domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Beneficial owner or duly authorized board of the foreign shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for each contributing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Audited bank or credit institution in the jurisdiction of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners against the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance sanctions list, United Nations consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and the domestic Luxembourg PEP registry. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP, and the compliance file must be maintained at the registered office and produced to the CSSF or other competent authorities upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) online portal — https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be legally compliant in French, German or Luxembourgish; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for registration. Names containing English or international terms must include a sufficient local descriptor and must not cause confusion with existing RCS registered enterprises.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice within 15 days of the rejection notice, attaching the RCS negative search certificate and a reasoned statement of compliance. The Ministry may consult the RCS Registrar before issuing a binding decision. A further judicial appeal before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg is available within three months of the Ministry decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted. A Luxembourg SARL must maintain a real and physical registered office located in Luxembourg. Virtual office addresses are rejected by the RCS. Shared or serviced executive offices are acceptable only where there is genuine local substance and a physical presence capable of receiving official correspondence and inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: approximately 15% risk of unannounced on-site inspection within the first two accounting years for a low-risk no-code website builder entity. The risk increases if tax authorities, the RCS, or AML authorities identify abnormal capital movements, negative substance indicators, or inconsistency with the declared commercial activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 710-1-1 et seq. governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and the Résultats, Enregistrement, Sécurité et Informatique system.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) with coordinated articles of association (statuts coordonnés), filed electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL requires a minimum subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000. The capital must be fully paid in cash at incorporation into a blocked bank account opened in the company name; the bank account release occurs only after RCS registration. Contributions in kind require a statutory auditor's valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders of Luxembourg SARL, duly convened, hereby resolve: (i) the subscription and full payment of 12,000 registered shares of one euro each, constituting the minimum capital, such funds being deposited in a blocked bank account in the company's name for release upon registration; (ii) the adoption of the registered office at [address], Luxembourg; (iii) the appointment of [Name] as manager (gérant) with sole signature powers; (iv) the shareholders' meeting reserves the right to amend the articles of association; and (v) the manager is authorized to execute all filings with the Trade and Companies Register and to publish in the RESA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name and Obtain Name-Availability Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers online portal (lbr.lu; RCS e-services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an electronic name-reservation request stating the proposed corporate name and the legal form SARL. Verify that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names and does not contain regulated terms. Receive an RCS name-availability certificate valid for a limited period and usable before the notary.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and legal form 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée'
Identity details of the applicant or incorporation vehicle
Declaration of eligibility where a regulated word is included
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, promptly file an amended request offering two alternative names. No prior fee is lost if the re-filing occurs before the name certificate expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Blocked Capital Account and Deposit the Minimum Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or bank selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the intended company name and deposit at least EUR 12,000 representing the fully paid minimum capital. Instruct the bank to issue a blocking certificate or unblocking confirmation addressed to the civil-law notary, and to maintain the funds blocked until RCS registration is completed. Ensure the account title exactly matches the reserved corporate name.
required_dossiers: RCS name-availability certificate
Draft articles of association or incorporation plan
Passport or national identity card of each shareholder and proposed manager
Proof of residential address of each shareholder and manager
Bank KYC and anti-money-laundering forms including UBO declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC information, provide a clear shareholding chart and a written description of the no-code software business. If the company name changes after a refused RCS reservation, request a new blocked-account certificate reflecting the corrected name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Notarial Deed and Coordinated Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notaire) practicing in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary, physically or by valid power of attorney, together with all shareholders and the proposed manager. The notary verifies the legal identity of all parties, reviews the coordinated articles, confirms that the minimum capital is blocked in accordance with the bank attestation, and reads the deed. Execute the notarial act and obtain certified copies for subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Notarized mandate or proxy if a shareholder cannot appear
Bank blocked-capital certificate
Draft coordinated articles of association
RCS name-availability certificate
Valid identity documents of all shareholders and managers
Proof of registered office address, such as lease agreement or letter of availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects omissions or irregularities, amend the coordinated articles and schedule a new execution time. If a shareholder fails to appear without valid proxy, supplementary signature pages must be notarized or the deed re-executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File with the RCS and Obtain Registration and RESA Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the notarial deed and coordinated articles electronically with the RCS immediately after execution. LBR examines the submission, verifies registered office and manager eligibility, assigns the RCS registration number, and issues an RCS extract. The incorporation particulars and the notarial deed are published in the RESA, making the company effective against third parties.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation and coordinated articles
Statement on the absence of criminal disqualification for each manager
Written acceptance of office signed by each manager
Proof of registered office if not contained in the deed
Bank blocked-capital certificate or notary's confirmation of capital payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS raises a query, the notary submits a rectification memorandum or an additional notarial act correcting the challenged point. If publication is delayed, follow up with LBR and supply any missing translation of the articles into the court language.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Direct Corporate Taxation and Value Added Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate registration with ACD to obtain the Luxembourg tax file number and fulfill direct tax obligations. Submit a separate VAT registration to AEDT where the SARL will make taxable supplies of services or acquire goods subject to Luxembourg VAT. State the principal activity as development and provision of no-code visual website-building software under ISIC 6201.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Notarial deed and coordinated articles of incorporation
Identity documents of manager and ultimate beneficial owners
Description of business activities and estimated turnover
VAT registration form and supporting schedules as required by AEDT
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authorities issue a query, re-submit the requested information and request adjustment of the effective tax registration dates. If VAT registration is disputed based on turnover projections, provide a written business plan with realistic revenue estimates and obtain a written ruling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Beneficial Ownership Declaration and Complete Physical Office Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers beneficial ownership register (RBE) for UBO filing; Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM) and the local commune for occupational and building clearance if a physical office is occupied
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the statutory beneficial ownership declaration to the RBE register within one month of registration, identifying every natural person who directly or indirectly holds more than 25% of share capital or voting rights. If a physical registered office or employee workplace is established, obtain the commune fire-safety certificate and, when applicable, register the premises and safety arrangements with ITM.
required_dossiers: RBE electronic declaration with UBO identification data
Passport or ID of each natural-person beneficial owner
Corporate organizational chart showing shareholding chains
Copy of lease or ownership title and fire-safety certificate for the registered office
Occupational health and safety declaration for any employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE declaration is queried, correct the UBO data and refile promptly to avoid fines. If the fire-safety inspection identifies defects, implement the required measures and schedule a re-inspection. For office-only software activity, no industrial environmental license is required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the no-code website-builder business under ISIC 6201 does not constitute industrial or manufacturing activity. General administrative oversight for software activities is exercised by the Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy and the competent municipal administration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operating, manufacturing, or commercial-operating license is required for a no-code visual website builder under Luxembourg law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environment Agency of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is a software and web-tool service with no physical installation, no classified installation, and no environmental permit requirement under the Luxembourg environmental classification rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated. General municipal effluent and waste-disposal standards for commercial offices under the amended Law of 19 December 2008 on waste and the Environment Act apply only where office sanitation or construction is concerned.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification of the registered office is required from the competent communal fire authority. Structural-load and building-occupancy clearance is required only when a physical office is leased; the local commune issues the occupancy certificate. For any employees, occupational-safety registration must be made with the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM). No civil-defense license is required for software-only activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg direct tax authority; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Luxembourg VAT and registration duties authority. Both operate through the national e-government portal MyGuichet.lu (www.myguichet.lu) and the AEDT secure VAT e-filing platform; official references: acd.public.lu and aedt.public.lu. The two administrations are in a legislated merger process toward a unified Luxembourg fiscal administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg-resident SARL, the national matricule (TIN) is assigned automatically upon notarial incorporation and filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through MyGuichet.lu. For a foreign entity without a Luxembourg establishment, VAT registration in Luxembourg is obtained by filing Application Form 1021 (Demande de numéro d'identification à la TVA) via MyGuichet.lu with the AEDT, attaching certified articles of association, proof of foreign tax registration, identity documents of legal representatives, and evidence of the intended taxable supplies; a Luxembourg tax representative must be appointed where required by law for non-established suppliers. VAT number format: LU + 8 digits; processing time generally 2–4 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Luxembourg SARL is a fully tax-opaque resident corporation: it is subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) on its worldwide profits, with treaty-based territorial relief for foreign permanent establishments and qualifying participation exemptions. The SARL is not eligible for partnership-style pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections: (i) group taxation / fiscal integration — election by a resident parent directly or indirectly holding at least 95% of a subsidiary's shares and voting rights, with a binding five-year commitment period and a minimum 95% integration ratio; (ii) VAT grouping as a single taxable person (assujetti unique) subject to AEDT approval for closely linked entities; (iii) OSS/IOSS special schemes for EU distance sales and digital B2C services; (iv) optional recharacterisation and adjustment elections required to comply with ATAD hybrid mismatch rules, with DAC6 mandatory disclosure obligations where applicable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Luxembourg value added tax (TVA / Mehrwertsteuer), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law (Loi TVA) implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (exclusive of VAT) annual turnover threshold for the small-enterprise VAT exemption in Luxembourg; VAT registration becomes mandatory from the first euro of turnover exceeding EUR 35,000. Non-established suppliers of digital services and distance sellers have no local registration threshold: they must account for Luxembourg VAT from the first taxable supply unless they use the OSS/IOSS scheme; digital no-code/SaaS B2C supplies are taxable where the consumer is established.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No comprehensive national B2B electronic-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance mandate currently applies in Luxembourg; there is no digital stamping or continuous transaction controls regime. B2G e-invoicing to Luxembourg public authorities is mandatory in PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 format (phased in from 2024). VAT returns, EC Sales Lists, and OSS filings must be submitted electronically through MyGuichet.lu / AEDT systems; the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' initiative will introduce standardised EU-wide B2B e-invoicing and digital reporting obligations around 2030, with Luxembourg transposition pending.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% VAT rate applies to: (a) export of goods physically dispatched or transported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU, evidenced by a customs export declaration and transport documentation in the name of the supplier or its behalf; (b) intra-Community supplies of goods where the goods are transported to another EU Member State, the customer is a VAT-registered operator, and the customer's EU VAT number is validated (VIES); (c) specified services directly connected with exported/imported goods (e.g. freight, handling, ancillary transport services). Digital no-code/SaaS subscriptions do not qualify as goods exports: B2B services to non-EU business customers fall outside Luxembourg VAT under place-of-supply rules; B2B services to EU customers are reverse-charged; B2C digital services are taxed at the consumer's EU Member State via OSS. The supplier must retain complete, chronological, verifiable evidence of the export chain to sustain the 0% rate upon audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / electronic ECS declaration in the Union Customs Code environment)
Transport documentation proving departure from the EU — Bill of Lading (sea), CMR/air waybill or equivalent
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank transfer confirmation evidencing receipt of the export consideration
Commercial invoice, sales contract, and EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) where ancillary to the transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where zero-rating is claimed without complete export/transport proof, the AEDT may retroactively assess VAT at the standard rate (17%) from the invoice date, disallow associated input VAT deductions, and charge statutory late-payment interest. Administrative penalties for defective or false documentation range from EUR 50 to EUR 4,000 per offence and are doubled for repetition. In cases of fraudulent export zero-rating, the administration may impose penalties of up to 200% of the evaded VAT, and criminal liability (fines and imprisonment) under the Luxembourg Criminal Code can be pursued. The AEDT conducts post-clearance audits using customs data and EU administrative cooperation (Regulation (EU) No 904/2010) to detect fictitious or sham exports; taxpayers must maintain all export and banking records in Luxembourg for inspection for at least the statutory 10-year retention period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB); credit-institution supervision and AML/CFT enforcement are delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), which issues banking licensing, prudential supervision, and compliance directives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies. Luxembourg has no foreign-exchange control statute, no central bank approval for foreign investment, and both capital-account and current-account transactions are liberalised under Article 63 TFEU, Luxembourg's long-standing policy of full liberalisation since the abolition of exchange controls in the early 1990s, and its OECD commitments. Inbound equity, shareholder loans, licence fees, and dividends may be freely credited or debited in EUR or any other convertible currency. Profit remittance is not FX-restricted; the only practical hurdles are (i) the Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (15% standard, 0% for qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or an applicable tax treaty), (ii) AML source-of-funds verification by the paying bank, and (iii) the statutory requirement to have financial statements approved by the shareholders' meeting confirming distributable reserves before a dividend distribution. No BCL or CSSF authorisation is required for a routine dividend payout.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg and the Eurosystem impose no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no statutory repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio. The de facto rule is a zero-day holding period and a 0% mandatory conversion ratio; the SARL may retain export proceeds in EUR, USD, or any freely convertible currency. The sole substantive compliance requirement is statistical: under EU Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 and BCL balance-of-payments instructions, Luxembourg credit institutions report cross-border payment details for resident non-banks, with the BCL's declarative threshold at EUR 12,500 per reporting item. This is a data-reporting obligation imposed on banks, not an exchange-control restriction affecting the SARL.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability, with clear legal subordination. Paddle and Stripe Treasury operate as EEA-authorised Payment Institutions or E-Money Institutions under PSD2 (Directive (EU) 2015/2366) and may lawfully extend a segregated client-money account to the Luxembourg SARL for card acquiring, subscription billing, and cross-border payouts through their partner settlement banks. However, an EMI is not a credit institution under the CRD framework and does not provide deposit-guarantee protection (DGSD EUR 100,000) for the SARL's balances; client funds are pooled and ring-fenced, creating counterparty and insolvency exposure. The CSSF expects the SARL to maintain its principal treasury, statutory capital, and VAT payments in a fully licensed EEA bank. Practical recommendation: retain Stripe/Paddle solely as collection and disbursement rails and run an automated daily SEPA/API sweep of balances into the BGL BNP Paribas or BIL operational account; do not rely on a third-country EMI (for example, a UK or UAE digital bank) as the primary treasury because post-Brexit passporting limitations and CSSF/bank KYC concerns will create friction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is strongly expected but not always mandatory. Under the amended Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF guidance on remote client onboarding, a credit institution may onboard a corporate client through certified video identification (passport verification, liveness check, geolocation) followed by documentary verification; in practice, BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, and Société Générale Bank & Trust require at least one in-person meeting at the Luxembourg branch or at a Luxembourg embassy/consulate for the ultimate beneficial owner(s) and one authorised signatory, or alternatively a notarised/apostilled KYC pack executed before a Luxembourg notary or a foreign notary under the Hague Apostille Convention. The managing director and each UBO holding at least 25% of the SARL must produce a valid passport and proof of residential address; if the director is not a UBO, a certified extract from the Luxembourg trade register (RCS) and a board resolution granting signature authority are required. Remote-only opening is available at ING Luxembourg and certain digital desks, but approval is discretionary and the process lengthens to four to eight weeks; the standard in-person route takes two to three weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO transparency gap: the SARL is owned through a chain of foreign holding companies or a corporate service provider, so the bank cannot identify the natural person exercising control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete shareholding cascade from the SARL to every natural-person UBO; the Luxembourg RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing confirmation; apostilled certificates of incorporation and registers of members for each intermediate entity; statutory declarations identifying controllers; and, where any intermediate entity is located in a FATF grey-listed jurisdiction, audited financial statements and evidence of the underlying commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial EUR 12,000 minimum share capital and any shareholder loan, particularly when funding originates from a related party or from significant cryptocurrency holdings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements for the remitting account; the notarised capital-subscription resolution and the bank's blocked-account certificate; an executed intercompany loan agreement if applicable; passport and source-of-wealth questionnaire for the investor; audited financial statements or tax returns of the corporate parent; and, for crypto-derived funds, conversion chain reports from a MiCA-authorised or equivalent regulated exchange.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-profile mismatch: the company is described generically as IT consulting, concealing the no-code SaaS subscription model, which the bank may flag as a potential invoice-mill or missing-trader fraud.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the signed merchant agreements with Stripe and Paddle; the ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 activity description; the URL of the live no-code builder platform; sample customer invoices and subscriber dashboards; Luxembourg VAT registration confirmation; a legal opinion or CSSF confirmation that the no-code website builder is not a regulated activity under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector; and a 12-month revenue forecast and cash-flow budget evidencing entity-level substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-profile mismatch with thin capitalisation: cross-border revenues from thousands of small-value subscriptions appear disproportionate to the SARL's EUR 12,000 capital base and minimal payroll, triggering a structured-entity review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written treasury and cash-flow policy aligned with the board-approved budget; platform analytics showing monthly run-rate, refund rates, and average subscription ticket; transfer-pricing documentation (Luxembourg TP Circular and OECD Chapter VI) proving that the SARL performs strategic functions, owns the software IP, and bears relevant economic risks; and a copy of the operational cost forecast (hosting, marketing, payroll) explaining the capitalisation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share capital: remit EUR via SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA zone) or SWIFT MT103 (non-SEPA) to the SARL's blocked capital-subscription account at a Luxembourg credit institution, using an ISO 20022 purpose code acceptable to the bank for equity contributions (typically EQUI, or INTC for intragroup capital movements) and including the required originator data under Regulation (EU) 2015/847; the remitter name must match the registered shareholder exactly, and the beneficiary reference field must quote the SARL's RCS registration number. The blocked funds are released only upon the Luxembourg notary's certificate confirming payment of the minimum share capital and filing of the incorporation deed. Shareholder loans: use a separate MT103 with purpose code LOAN, attach the executed intercompany loan agreement with an arm's-length interest rate, and document the source of funds with 12 months of bank statements. Banks automatically file BCL balance-of-payments statistical declarations for cross-border amounts above the EUR 12,500 threshold; no central bank or CSSF approval is required for the inbound capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For recurring software/API, hosting, and marketing payments inside the EEA, use SEPA Credit Transfers in EUR with ISO purpose code SOFT (Software) or ROYL (Royalties) to the vendor's IBAN; for non-EEA vendors, instruct SWIFT MT103 in EUR with payment method CRED and charge option SHA, accompanied by the same purpose code and the commercial invoice reference. For bundled hardware or physical-device procurement under the ISIC 6201 scope, use open-account settlement against pro-forma invoices, or an irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit (UCP 600, SWIFT MT700) only when contractually required; typical LC documents are the commercial invoice, transport document, packing list, and certificate of origin. Outbound USD payments flow through the bank's USD clearing chain with a correspondent bank and must include an invoice reference to avoid compliance holds. Stripe/Paddle payouts settle in EUR to the SARL's IBAN after the platform converts USD at its wholesale rate; to minimise FX leakage, the SARL should invoice customers in EUR and maintain a sub-ledger for platform settlement fees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD deliverable forwards (tenor up to 24 months) executed under the bank's ISDA 2002 Master Agreement plus a Credit Support Annex or the bank's standard treasury terms
FX swaps (spot/forward rolls) for converting USD subscription proceeds to EUR without maintaining an overnight open position
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted currencies (e.g., CNH, INR, KRW) if Stripe/Paddle route payments in those currencies from cross-border cardholders

Plain vanilla purchased EUR/USD options (long call or long put) to cap conversion cost on USD-denominated marketing spend while retaining upside; writing options is not recommended for SARL treasury policy
Overnight spot conversion via the bank's electronic FX platform ring-fenced by a board-approved risk limit and daily stop-loss; no speculative derivative positions are permitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Bilan, Compte de Profits et Pertes, Annexe) filing with the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registrar of Commerce and Companies (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end for shareholder approval, followed by filing with the RCS within 1 month of approval (typical effective deadline: 31 May for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Referral to the District Court by the Public Prosecutor; administrative and criminal fines of €750–€2,500 per director or manager; repeated non-compliance may trigger a judicial strike-off (radiation) of the SARL

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 351) including Net Wealth Tax (impôt sur la fortune) and Municipal Business Tax (impôt commercial communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the year following the tax year for paper filing; extended to 31 December of the same year for electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on outstanding tax; late filing administrative fine up to €3,750; ex officio assessment with a 10% surcharge if the return is not filed within one month of formal reminder

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs — RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; any change in beneficial ownership (e.g., share transfer) must be declared within one month of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal sanctions of 8 days to 3 years imprisonment and fines of €10,000–€250,000; additional administrative fines of €500–€5,000 per infraction; publication of the judicial decision against the entity

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is mandatory where the SARL exceeds at least two of the three following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total €6.25 million, net turnover €12.5 million, average of 250 employees. A 'small' undertaking (per the Law of 19 December 2020) is exempt; a typical no-code SaaS builder below these thresholds is exempt from mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan comptable normalisé per the Law of 19 December 2020) for statutory annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for consolidated accounts and may be applied voluntarily to individual accounts where not prohibited.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Pursuant to the Law of 13 January 2019 (as amended on 19 December 2020), the SARL must keep the RBE register continuously accurate; beneficial owners holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of shares or voting rights must be identified and kept current. An annual confirmation filing is mandatory on the anniversary of registration, and any share transfer or change in control must be declared to the RBE within one month.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Register des actionnaires / des parts sociales)
Register of Directors and Managers (minutes of management and shareholder resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 (statutory exemption applying to the small undertaking) — 5,000 to 12,000 if a voluntary or Portugal non-applicable audit is engaged

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% (2024) on taxable income exceeding EUR 175,000; 15% on the first EUR 175,000; from FY 2025 the schedule becomes 16% above EUR 200,000. Add the 7% Employment Fund solidarity surcharge on CIT and municipal business tax (6.75% in Luxembourg City), yielding a combined marginal effective rate of approximately 24.94% (2024) / 23.87% (2025) in Luxembourg City.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. Key reductions: (i) participation exemption (100% of qualifying dividends and capital gains where the SARL holds >=10% or an acquisition cost >= EUR 1.2M for an uninterrupted 12 months); (ii) notional interest deduction on qualifying new cash equity; (iii) 8% supplementary investment tax credit; (iv) progressive 15%/17% (16% from 2025) CIT bands for smaller bases. The former IP box was repealed with effect from 1 January 2021 (grandfathering ended 30 June 2024), so a no-code/website-builder SaaS model cannot rely on the old 80% IP income exemption unless grandfathered.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1002 - Declaration for corporate income tax (covering CIT, the 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax), filed electronically via the eCDF module of MyGuichet.lu with LU-COSI authentication or through a licensed Luxembourg fiduciary. Net wealth tax is assessed on the separate annual Form 1003.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Calendar-year SARLs: return due by 31 December of the year following the tax year (e.g., FY 2024 by 31 December 2025); non-calendar accounting periods: due by 31 December of the year following the closing date, with extensions on reasoned request. Quarterly CIT prepayments are due 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS Luxembourg number, VAT number, registered office, and the competent tax office (bureau d'imposition) reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SARL is a Luxembourg tax resident through its registered office and central administration; the managing director (gerant) must be named as contact; foreign shareholders appear only in the participations schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year-end date and confirmation that the accounts cover a 12-month period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep the Luxembourg accounting period synchronous with the parent's consolidation; a non-calendar parent cycle does not excuse late filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet per Luxembourg GAAP: share capital, retained earnings, intercompany receivables/payables, cash and deferred items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all intercompany balances in the annex; bare-shell balance sheets with no employees or premises invite substance review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D - Compte de profits et pertes (P&L)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory net accounting result, including third-party and intra-group revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize no-code SaaS subscription revenue on an accrual basis regardless of the settlement date of Stripe/Paddle payouts; unreported foreign-currency balances are evident discrepancies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible add-backs: disallowed entertainment, fines, certain manager fees, and the non-deductible interest portion under ATAD (excess interest above 30% EBITDA safe harbour).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to the foreign parent beyond the safe harbour must be added back; keep ATAD ratio computations signed and dated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: participation exemption, notional interest deduction, investment credits, and other deductible provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the participation exemption, attach the foreign subsidiary's tax-residence certificate and holding-period proof; for NID, evidence the cash injection and the 5-month holding rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all add-backs and deductions; must reconcile to Section D.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A variance above 10% against the statutory result triggers automatic review; prepare a reconciliation note.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section G - Box 330 (CIT, solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of 15%/17% CIT (16%/15% from 2025), 7% solidarity surcharge, and municipal business tax at the commune rate (6.75% Luxembourg City).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The commune is that of the registered office; credits and prepayments are recognized only when actually paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year losses absorbed against current income within the 17-year carryforward window.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A change of more than 50% of the SARL's shares within 12 months extinguishes the carryforward unless continuity of the business is demonstrated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section I - Balance due and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly prepayments declared and residual CIT payable after offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the residual within one month of the assessment; unpaid balances accrue 0.6% monthly interest (7.2% per annum).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing: administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 plus a 10% surcharge on the assessed tax; late payment: 0.6% monthly interest on amounts outstanding; fraudulent suppression: criminal fines from EUR 2,500 to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years, with publication of convictions possible.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1003 (annual net wealth tax return) - filed electronically alongside Form 1002 via the eCDF/MyGuichet.lu portal; net wealth tax at 0.5% on net asset value (minimum EUR 535 or EUR 3,500 depending on balance-sheet size).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same fiscal-inscription cycle as Form 1002: due 31 December of the year following the tax year, subject to the same extension practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Luxembourg and foreign assets after depreciation and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Unitary basis with no worldwide consolidation; intercompany loans to the parent are subject to 0.5% unless the 12-month participation exemption applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying shareholdings (>=10% or EUR 1.2M) excluded from the net wealth base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same substance and holding-period conditions as the CIT participation exemption apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result after participation relief and EUR 500,000 exempt allowance for businesses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The allowance and minimum tax apply at entity level; no consolidation with the foreign parent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and understatement trigger the same regime as Form 1002: fine up to EUR 25,000, 10% surcharge, 0.6% monthly interest; deliberate omission is treated as tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on Luxembourg-source dividends paid by a SARL; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the corporate beneficial owner holds >=10% or a EUR 1.2M acquisition cost for at least 12 months and is a qualifying EU/EEA resident; 0% for Luxembourg-resident corporate shareholders under the domestic parent-subsidiary regime; treaty rates generally 5%-15% (e.g., 5% under many DTAs for holdings above 10%, 15% portfolio) subject to the principal-purpose test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief is claim-based, not automatic. The Luxembourg paying SARL (or the foreign recipient) must file the exemption/reduction request with the ACD via the electronic eCDF procedure attaching: (i) the foreign tax-residence certificate (TRC) of the beneficiary issued by its competent authority and certified within 12 months, (ii) the completed standard ACD exemption form, (iii) evidence of shareholding size and holding period, and (iv) a brief economic-substance narrative where the beneficial owner is an intermediate holding company. Processing normally takes 3-6 months; where the TRC is pending, the recipient may obtain a refund by reclaim after the distribution subject to the same documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic rate is 0%: Luxembourg imposes no withholding tax on outbound royalties and no withholding tax on outbound interest, including payments to non-resident associated companies. The EU Interest & Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC) conditions (25% direct shareholding for 24 months) are therefore only relevant for EU source claims in the counterparty State. No DTA application is triggered for Luxembourg-source payments; anti-abuse review still applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory where intra-group transactions within one category exceed EUR 100,000 per year (financial transactions, IP transfers and licences, goods, services, management fees) or EUR 50,000 for guarantee transactions. Master File and Country-by-Country Report: for groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million. Defensive documentation and a benchmarking study are recommended for a no-code SaaS SARL even below the thresholds, and are required for any APA or unilateral ruling request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate UAE/BVI-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substance is enforced through the statutory general anti-abuse rule (Article 6 of the 1934 Tax Adaptation Law, reinforced by the 2016 reform), the EU ATAD interest-limitation and anti-hybrid rules, and the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test applicable to DTAs. A SARL carrying the no-code website-builder business must maintain premises, a Luxembourg-based gerant taking commercial decisions, employees or contractors whose number and skill profile correspond to the activity, and contemporaneous board minutes. Absent such substance, the ACD may ignore the Luxembourg entity, reattribute its profits to the foreign parent, deny treaty and directive benefits, and extend the assessment period from 5 to 11 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion - suppression of subscription revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting no-code SaaS revenue collected through Stripe/Paddle, maintaining undeclared foreign accounts or dual invoicing sets, or assisting a foreign parent in shifting profits through fake license fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment plus late/incomplete-return fine up to EUR 25,000, 10% surcharge, 0.6% monthly interest, and criminal prosecution under Article 392 ff. LIR: imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and fines of EUR 2,500 to EUR 50,000, with the court able to order publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gerant or director who signs a knowingly false return is jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax, penalties and interest; personal assets can be seized, and the court may impose a management ban applicable across the EU through mutual recognition.
